relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover (arXiv:2601.05136v2, 15 May 2026, state integrals for the quantized SL_2(C) Chern-Simons invariant, single author, Duke) and matches the seeded key, including the ref() note's v2/May-2026 detail. Citation status is NOT 'cited': the ref() entry exists (references.ts:5249) but grep over content/ finds no `\cite{}`, no `[mcphail-snyder2026]` and no cites-array entry — a bib orphan. Its only appearance is docs/audits/2026-08-01-fantini-wheeler-summability-c3-borel-reframe.md:109, the audit that also handled fantini-wheeler2024; that audit's Lean output (BorelStateIntegralSummability.lean, StateIntegralRecursionLattice.lean) cites fantini-wheeler2024 only. So it was gathered alongside a landed reference and did not land itself. Its subject is directly adjacent: it expresses the geometric-twist / quantized SL_2(C) Chern-Simons invariant Z^psi_N(K, rho, mu) as a sum over contour integrals in a space parametrising hyperbolic structures on the knot complement — i.e. a state-integral presentation of a Kashaev-type invariant built from quantum dilogarithms, which is the same machinery the corpus's state-integral files use. Supporting rather than core: no corpus block currently consumes one of its statements, and I have not checked whether its state-integral presentation is compatible with the Andersen-Kashaev presentation the corpus's other source uses.

proposedActions.rationale: The reference is recorded and its audit context is documented. Citing it would require first checking that its state-integral presentation and the Andersen-Kashaev one used by the corpus's landed source describe the same object under a stated normalisation; asserting adjacency without that check is what the corpus's citation-drift problems are made of.
